title: Where do you meet human rights in an ordinary day?
examples: What are human rights in everyday life?
Which human rights do I use every day?
Examples of human rights at school

explain.say: Human rights sound like something for courts and presidents, far away. But you meet them from the moment you wake up! Look at the board: one ordinary day, from breakfast to bedtime. Human rights are the basic freedoms and protections every person has, just for being human.

explain.say: See 7 am, breakfast? The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, agreed in 1948, says everyone has a right to food, clothing and a home, in Article 25. Then at 8 am, school: Article 26 says everyone has a right to education. Why do you think school made the list?

explain.say: Now look at 11 am, speak your mind. When you share your opinion in class, or write a story, you are using freedom of expression, Article 19. It also means listening when others disagree. And at 1 pm, you may pray in your own way, or not at all: that is freedom of religion. Can you spot your favourite right?

explain.say: See 4 pm, a doctor visit, and 9 pm, a safe home? Health care and privacy are rights too. Privacy means others should not read your diary or barge into your home without good reason. Which of these rights did you use yesterday?

explain.say: Rights come with responsibilities: your right to speak goes with respecting others' rights too. Sadly, not everyone gets all these rights yet, which is why people keep working for them. Great job! Challenge: tomorrow, count how many rights you use before lunch.

faq.a: Human rights are basic freedoms and protections that belong to every person, everywhere, just for being human, like the right to life, education, fair treatment and free speech. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights listed 30 of them in 1948.
Yes. Article 25 of the Universal Declaration says everyone has the right to a standard of living good enough for health and well-being, including food, clothing, housing and medical care.
Yes. Article 26 says everyone has the right to education, and that basic education should be free and compulsory.
asks: Do all children have a right to school?

faq.a: Freedom of expression, Article 19, is the right to hold opinions and share ideas by speaking, writing or art. Most countries set some limits, such as on threats or lies that harm others, and people debate where those limits should be.
asks: Tell me about speak your mind
Is free speech a human right?

faq.q: What is the right to privacy?
faq.a: Article 12 says nobody should interfere without good reason with your privacy, family, home or letters and messages. It protects your private life.
asks: Do children have a right to privacy?

facts: The UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948, now marked as Human Rights Day.
The UDHR has 30 articles and is one of the most translated documents in the world, available in over 500 languages.
Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the UN commission that drafted it; India's Hansa Mehta helped change "all men" to "all human beings" in Article 1.

quiz.say: You write an opinion piece for the school newsletter. Which right are you using?
quiz.show: Sharing your opinion uses the right to…
quiz.why: Sharing your ideas and opinions is freedom of expression, Article 19.

wrong.0: Privacy protects your private life, not your sharing.
wrong.2: The right to food is about having enough to eat.

quiz.say: When was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights agreed?
quiz.why: The UN adopted it on 10 December 1948, after the Second World War.

wrong.0: 1848 was a century too early; the UN did not exist.
